newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek shares slip on weak banks, industrials.
newsitem.headline: Greek shares slip on weak banks, industrials.

text.p: Greek shares finished 0.61 percent lower on price weakness in banks and industrials but came off mid-session lows and fund managers attributed the market's weak performance to uncertainty regarding interest rates.

Bucking the trend, new listing Epiphania which went public at 1,600 drachmas, jumped 29.3 percent to 2,070 drachmas in its trade debut. Volume reached 256,510 shares, nearly three quarters of its total 350,000-share offering.
Epiphania is a specialist in business publications and print communications.

"Investors are side-stepping price shifts caused by external influences and sentiment remains cautious. In view of fiscal requirements estimated at around 6.0 trillion drachmas until year-end the scope for lower interest rates is shaky," said Thomas Loukeris, fund manager at Macedonia-Thrace Bank's Vergina mutual funds.
On Monday, the Bank of Greece cut 30 basis points off its base deposit facility rate to 11.30 percent, leaving the floor rate unchanged at 9.60 percent.
The finance ministry also cut 10 basis points from its 12-month T-bills to be offered to the public on August 20, followed by an auction of 100 billion drachmas of FRNs on August 21.
"The government and the Bank of Greece are testing the market with their rate cuts ahead of larger issues of treasury paper in coming months," said Loukeris.
"It is a strategy move as the finance ministry has opted for external financing and there are growing indications that the Fed and the Bundesbank will not alter their rates," he added.
The Athens benchmark index settled 0.61 percent or 9.88 points lower at 1,613.02 from Monday's 1,622.90 close, oscillating between 1,607 and 1,630 points.
Banks and industrials drifted 0.73 and 0.70 percent lower, respectively, but other sectors posted milder losses.
Turnover was boosted to 11.9 billion drachmas on volume of 2.6 million shares by block trades in blue chips and active trade in bourse newcomer Epiphania.
Block trades included OTE telecom, 69,046 shares at 6,600 drachmas, Alpha Credit Bank, 30,000 shares at 19,900, and Attica Enterprises, 100,000 shares at 2,900.
Decliners outpaced advancers 108 to 86 with 18 shares unchanged on 212 traded.
OTE telecom Global Depository Shares (GDS) were quoted on London's SEAQ International market at $11.1-$11.5. Two GDSs make up one share of OTE.
The Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 3,800 drachmas, capped at 5,000 drachmas, was quoted at 1,132-1,162 drachmas.

The recently launched second Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 6,800 drachmas, capped at 10,000 drachmas, was quoted at 1,110-1,170 drachmas. The warrants expire December 16, 1998. Shares of the underlying stock fell 15 drachmas to 6,595.
The Merrill Lynch American call warrant on a basket of 23 Greek equities that are part of the Athens general index was quoted at 661.02-703.21 drachmas. The warrants expire January 9 1998.

The ING Baring Financial Products American style call warrant based on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted at $74.05-$76.84. The strike price is set at $99.60 and the warrants expire October 8, 1997.

The ING Baring Financial Products American-style call warrant on a basket of six blue-chips denominated in drachmas was quoted at 3,735-3,963 drachmas. The strike price is set at 10,000 drachmas and the warrants expire on February 2, 1998.
The ING Baring American-style second call warrant on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted at $11.17 bid/no offer. The strike price is set at $110.0 and the warrants expire April 9 1998.

The recently launched ING Baring American-style, drachma- denominated call warrant on the bourse's benchmark index was quoted at 222-254 drachmas. The strike price is set at 1,639 points and the warrants expire May 14 1998. --Angelos Kiosklis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
